title: ak pick --kinds --json (pick-v2)
description: The cross-kind priority pick for daemons (herdr-peers autopilot --loop and its agents): the FIRST kind of --kinds with a qualifying account, chosen by the same rows, cache and policy as pick-v1 (docs/usage.md#choosing-an-account). Read-only: no login is refreshed, no reset is spent. `launch.argv` is the exact interactive argv to start that agent, so a caller never learns any CLI's own flags; `model` is what the caller asked for that kind (resolution happens at launch). Never contains a secret value or an account identity. Consumers check `schema` and `interface` before reading anything else; additional top-level keys may appear in later minor versions.

qualifies.description: False on the no-qualifier form: the winner fields are null and launch.argv is null; a --json caller always gets a document, like pick-v1.

priority_index.description: The winning kind's index in `kinds` (0 = the first kind qualified); null when nothing qualifies.

kind.description: The winning kind as given in --kinds.

profile.description: Null only on the no-qualifier form.

model.description: --model-for for the winning kind, else --model, else null; resolved at launch, not here. A dash-leading value is refused at parse time.

argv.description: The exact interactive argv, e.g. ["ak","claude","@work","--model","sonnet"] — the model is head-level so it goes through the CLI's model_flag mapping, the models allowlist and the leading-dash check. Null on the no-qualifier form.

env_names.description: Environment variable NAMES the caller may need; empty on the default path (ak sets the CLI homes itself).

permissions.description: Which permission mode the argv implies: ak's default (auto — the CLI's own bypass flag) or ask when the pick ran with the opt-out. A caller that wants ask-mode launches appends ["--ask"] before any -- (a documented head flag); it never needs the CLI's own bypass flag.

lease.description: The active lease on the chosen account, if any (ak lease); null without one.

soonest_reset.description: ISO-8601 UTC: the earliest reset seen across the list; null when none is known.
